papers.titleEn: Ionization-State-Directed Sulfonate-Rich Buried Interfaces Enable Durable High-Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Proton‐triggered degradation at the buried interface severely undermines the operational stability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). To address this issue, this work develops an ionization‐state‐directed sulfonate approach using sodium 2,2'‐disulfanediyldiethanesulfonate (DDANA). The pre‐deprotonated sulfonate terminals grant DDANA strong coordination with lead sites and drive its spontaneous aggregation at the perovskite and self‐assembled monolayer interface, forming robust multisite binding with the perovskite lattice. The enriched sulfonate groups build favorable interfacial dipoles to optimize energy level alignment and facilitate hole transport. The immobilized sulfonate groups act as conjugate‐based sites to competitively capture protons, while the disulfide skeleton enables reversible iodine‐redox to scavenge corrosive iodine species under operational stress. Dissociated sodium (Na + ) ions embed into lattice interstices and release residual tensile strain. As a result, DDANA‐modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 27.38% (certified 27.13%). The strategy extends seamlessly to flexible devices and rigid large‐area modules, delivering efficiencies of 25.88% and 23.33%, respectively. Moreover, the DDANA‐modified devices retain 98.9% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking and 97.4% after cycling diurnals. This work establishes sulfonate ionization‐state engineering as a versatile molecular design platform for constructing chemically robust buried interfaces toward efficient, stable, and scalable perovskite photovoltaics.
papers.filename: Ziyi Ge, Adv. Mater., 2026, Ionization-State-Directed Sulfonate-Rich Buried Interfaces Enable Durable High-Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules

papers.titleEn: Eco-friendly synthesis of InSe nanoflakes for NO2 gas sensors with excellent response and high humidity resilience
papers.abstract: In this paper, a faster and more environmentally friendly way to produce Indium selenide (InSe) nanoflakes for NO 2 gas sensors utilizing a non-toxic solvent (IPA/DI water) is presented. A simple technique of Liquid Phase Exfoliation was employed for the synthesis of the sensing material. The as-produced InSe nanoflakes were subjected to structural, morphological and compositional analyses with FESEM, XRD, TEM, Raman spectroscopy, EDX, DLS and XPS. These samples were then used in the development of NO 2 gas sensors for real-world applications. Sensors were tested under several conditions, including optimal operating temperature, low NO 2 concentrations, and background humidity. Sensors outperform the state of the art, with a 149.10% response for 1 ppm of NO 2 at an operating temperature of 200℃ and very low response and recovery times. Sensors also exhibit an enhanced response of 237.59% in the presence of 50% R.H. @ 25ºC, little humidity cross-sensitivity in the 25 to 75% R.H. range, with a low limit of detection of 35 ppb. Their high sensitivity and selectivity combined to their ability to operate under ambient moisture, make these sensors promising for monitoring traces of NO 2 in the ambient.
papers.filename: Eduard Llobet, Sens. Actuators B Chem., 2026, Eco-friendly synthesis of InSe nanoflakes for NO2 gas sensors with excellent response and high humidity resilience

papers.titleEn: Surfactant Induces Uniform and Stable Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have been extensively studied in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Nevertheless, the aggregation tendency of SAM molecules results in non‐uniform deposition and inadequate substrate coverage, thereby severely impeding device performance. Herein, we introduce a multifunctional additive, nonafluorobutane‐1‐sulfonic acid (PFBS), to actively regulate the growth of SAM layers. Our investigations reveal that PFBS suppresses the self‐aggregation of SAM molecules through hydrogen bonding and steric disruption, thus promoting their dispersion in the solution and facilitating the exposure of anchoring groups. The PFBS‐modified SAM exhibits improved coverage, robustness, and interfacial energy‐level alignment. Furthermore, PFBS effectively passivates interfacial defects, reduces non‐radiative recombination, and promotes the growth of high‐quality perovskite film. Consequently, the PFBS‐optimized PSC with a 1.68 eV bandgap delivers a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 24% and significantly enhanced stability. This work presents an additive‐induced ordering strategy, providing a scalable route for high‐performance PSCs and tandem photovoltaics.
papers.filename: Tanghao Liu, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Surfactant Induces Uniform and Stable Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Ionic Liquid-Functionalized CNT Electrochemical Platform Governed by a Dual-Path Sensing Mechanism for Versatile VOC Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract Room-temperature ionic liquids (RTILs) have garnered significant attention as advanced electrolytes for electrochemical gas sensors owing to their negligible volatility and wide electrochemical windows. However, their application in detecting volatile organic compounds (VOCs) is constrained by high viscosity (limiting mass transport) and the sluggish electrooxidation kinetics of most VOCs. Supported ionic liquid phase (SILP) materials, which immobilize RTILs on porous supports to amplify the gas–liquid interface, present a promising yet underexplored avenue for addressing these challenges. Herein, we develop a novel electrochemical platform configured with high-purity semiconducting carbon nanotube (CNT) films serving as both working electrodes and scaffolds to immobilize RTILs to construct a nanostructured SILP electrolyte. This architecture simultaneously maximizes the active gas–liquid interface, minimizes the gas diffusion distance, and ensures efficient charge transport. The platform enables quantitative detection of ethanol and isopropanol, exhibiting well-defined linear responses from 0–800 ppm and 0–600 ppm, respectively, with distinctive non-monotonic patterns at higher concentrations. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the sensing process diverges from conventional faradaic electrochemistry and is instead governed by a dual-path mechanism: competitive adsorption between oxygen and VOC molecules at the SILP surface, coupled with VOC absorption into the bulk phase. This unique mechanism, which circumvents the limitations of direct electrooxidation by exploiting distinct interactions between VOCs and the SILP, provides inherent discriminative capability. Consequently, our work establishes the CNT-SILP system as a versatile, miniaturization-ready platform for room-temperature VOC sensing and paves the way for novel intelligent gas sensors.
papers.filename: Qiliang Li, ACS Sens., 2026, Ionic Liquid-Functionalized CNT Electrochemical Platform Governed by a Dual-Path Sensing Mechanism for Versatile VOC Detection

papers.titleEn: Bandgap and Interface Engineering of Ag-Au-S Quantum Dots toward Bright Near-Infrared Emission and Deep-Tissue Bioimaging
papers.abstract: Abstract Low-toxicity colloidal quantum dots (QDs) with tunable near-infrared (NIR) emission are promising for bioimaging because biological tissues exhibit relatively low light scattering and absorption in the 700–1700 nm optical window. However, it remains challenging to achieve high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs), aqueous stability, and tunable emission simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate efficient NIR emission from Ag–Au–S QDs by combining composition control with heterointerface engineering. Varying the Ag/Au ratio tuned the bandgap from 1.39 to 1.88 eV and shifted the PL peak from 1130 to 745 nm. QDs prepared with an Ag/(Ag+Au) precursor ratio of 0.75 had an average diameter of 2.5 nm and consisted of a polycrystalline Ag3AuS2 core surrounded by an amorphous Ag–S-rich surface layer. These QDs exhibited a PL peak at 800 nm with a PLQY of 3.4%. In–S shell coating increased the PLQY to 33.6%. Subsequent ZnS treatment produced Janus-like Ag–Au–S@In–Zn–S QDs exhibiting a PL peak at 840 nm with a PLQY of 38.9%, consistent with suppression of nonradiative recombination through surface passivation. After ligand exchange with 3-mercaptopropionic acid, the QDs were readily dispersed in water while retaining a PLQY of 27.0% and exhibited excellent PL stability in biologically relevant media. The QDs enabled in vivo deep-tissue imaging, with NIR PL detected from tissues at depths of up to 15 mm. These findings demonstrate that Ag–Au–S-based QDs are promising low-toxicity NIR probes for biomedical imaging.
papers.filename: Tsukasa Torimoto, ACS Nano, 2026, Bandgap and Interface Engineering of Ag-Au-S Quantum Dots toward Bright Near-Infrared Emission and Deep-Tissue Bioimaging

papers.titleEn: Self-Calibrating Ratiometric Colorimetric Microfluidic Paper-Based Analytical Device for Visual Quantification of Hypoxanthine
papers.abstract: Abstract Existing self-calibrating strategies improve quantitative paper-based colorimetry by correcting imaging variations, yet their analytical reliability remains limited because heterogeneous sensing interfaces introduce errors that cannot be compensated by internal-reference calibration alone. Herein, we present a self-calibrating ratiometric microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs) based on a dual error-control strategy that integrates interface homogenization with internal-reference correction for portable hypoxanthine (Hx) quantification, an important early freshness indicator of aquatic products. A sol−gel/chitosan (Sol−Gel/CS) hybrid network uniformly immobilizes MnO2 nanoflowers (NFs), suppressing coffee-ring formation while improving reagent stability, catalytic activity, and color uniformity. Xanthine oxidase (XOD), incorporated only into the test zone, catalyzes Hx oxidation to generate H2O2 and uric acid, which decompose MnO2 NFs and weaken their oxidase-like activity toward 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine, producing an Hx-dependent color decrease. Meanwhile, the XOD-free reference zone provides a stable internal-reference signal. Ratiometric analysis (IT/IR) effectively compensates for imaging variations across different smartphones, enabling reliable visual quantification. The μPAD achieved a detection limit of 3.42 μM and agreed well with triple-quadrupole liquid chromatography−tandem mass spectrometry. Freshness monitoring of crucian carp, shrimp, and scallop was successfully demonstrated through both extract-based and direct-contact assays. This dual error-control strategy establishes a general framework for robust quantitative paper-based colorimetric sensing.
papers.filename: Xiaokun Wang, Anal. Chem., 2026, Self-Calibrating Ratiometric Colorimetric Microfluidic Paper-Based Analytical Device for Visual Quantification of Hypoxanthine

papers.titleEn: A Double-Excitation Intrinsically Dual Emissive Carbon Dot Platform Enables Multi-Channel Sensitive Detection and Imaging of Common Pesticides in Live Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Carbon dot sensors often couple one excitation condition to one analyte and one output, limiting information from a single probe. Here, we report intrinsically dual-emissive carbon dots (De-CDs) whose two excitation windows partition complementary sensing functions. Under 365 nm excitation, Hg2+ quenches the 450 and 680 nm emissions and clothianidin restores them, enabling sequential on-off-on determination by ratiometric fluorescence and a complementary UV−Vis response at 441 nm. The fluorescence channel quantified Hg2+ over 0.0116−12 μmol L−1 (LOD = 0.0116 μmol L−1), while clothianidin showed piecewise calibration up to 45 μmol L−1 (LOD = 0.0031 μmol L−1); UV−Vis LODs were 0.0095 and 0.0010 μmol L−1. The dual-channel design enables simultaneous utilization of fluorescent and UV wavelengths, thereby reducing interference and enhancing selectivity during detection. Under 420 nm excitation, a red-emission redistribution quantified Zn2+ over 0.0157−3.5 μmol L−1 (LOD = 0.0157 μmol L−1) and provided a zineb calibration over 0.0102−9 μmol L−1 (LOD = 0.0102 μmol L−1). Hg2+ forms ground-state complexes causing fluorescence quenching, and clothianidin competitively displaces Hg2+ to restore fluorescence (“On-Off-On”). In contrast, Zn2+ induces chelation-enhanced fluorescence by restricting intramolecular motion and suppressing non-radiative decay. Measurements in soil, river water, and fruit agreed with ICP-AES, LC−MS, or GC. Excitation-dependent responses were further demonstrated in HepG2 cells, zebrafish, mice, and rice seedlings. This carbon-dot scaffold separates sensing tasks by excitation wavelength and integrates complementary readouts with multiscale imaging. This multifunctional platform integrates environmental, common foods monitoring and bioimaging for synchronous analysis of multiple pollutants.
papers.filename: Fei Ye, Anal. Chem., 2026, A Double-Excitation Intrinsically Dual Emissive Carbon Dot Platform Enables Multi-Channel Sensitive Detection and Imaging of Common Pesticides in Live Mo

papers.titleEn: Breaking the 35% Efficiency Milestone: Material Innovations and Interface Mechanisms in Monolithic Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Crystalline silicon solar cells are approaching their theoretical Auger efficiency limit, necessitating tandem architectures that transcend the Shockley–Queisser constraint and lower the cost of electricity. Monolithic perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (PSTSCs) have breached the 35% power conversion efficiency barrier, emerging as the leading candidate to disrupt the photovoltaic landscape. However, translating this laboratory success to terawatt‐scale deployment requires precise control over charge transport and interfacial recombination at the interconnecting layer (ICL). This review examines the material innovations driving this evolution, grounded in a quantitative loss‐budget analysis, with a focus on the ICL and full‐dimensional interface engineering. We first examine the evolving ICL paradigm, from defect‐mediated transport in amorphous silicon to efficient band‐to‐band tunneling in polycrystalline silicon junctions, and the enhanced charge extraction enabled by transparent conductive oxides with self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs), whose Ohmic contact formation we trace through an anchoring‐to‐Fermi‐level‐depinning mechanism. We further dissect breakthroughs mitigating non‐radiative losses on textured silicon substrates, where SAMs and passivation strategies overcome steric hindrance and contact resistance, and where the same pyramid texture governs wide‐bandgap perovskite crystallization and its process‐engineering trade‐offs. Finally, we navigate the “efficiency‐stability‐cost” trilemma, addressing halide‐segregation and ion‐migration suppression under a standardized stability framework, alongside scalable manufacturing toward industrial translation.
papers.filename: Wei Ma, Adv. Funct. Mater., 2026, Breaking the 35% Efficiency Milestone Material Innovations and Interface Mechanisms in Monolithic Perovskite Silicon Tandem Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Addressing the 1000-h/1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs
papers.abstract: Abstract Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) offer exceptional colour purity and efficiency for next-generation display applications. Despite the recent advances in device stability, achieving long-term stable PeLEDs under display-relevant conditions remains a critical challenge. The actual device half-life (T 50 ) experimentally measured for visible PeLEDs were in most cases limited to below 1000 h for any given brightness, in contrast to the much longer extrapolated lifetimes reported. Here, we demonstrate stable green PeLEDs with a T 50 lifetime of 1350 h at an initial luminance of 1000 cd m −2 (nits), a maximum energy-conversion efficiency of 28.0%, and a peak external quantum efficiency of 24.5%. The exceptional performance is enabled by the insertion of a fluorinated self-assembled monolayer between the metal oxide and polymeric hole-transport layers. This molecular interlayer leads to Ohmic-like characteristics for charge injection, lowering the operating voltage at ~1000 nits to sub-bandgap levels (~2.1 V) where ion migration is suppressed. The accumulated photon output of our PeLEDs over the course of their T 50 lifespan is found to sharply increase as the driving voltage drops to sub-bandgap values, highlighting the critical role of employing low-voltage device architectures in reaching the 1350-h/1000-nit stability milestone. Finally, a flexible active-matrix PeLED display prototype is developed, showing the potential of the devices for wearable optoelectronics.
papers.filename: Dawei Di, Nat. Commun., 2026, Addressing the 1000-h 1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs

papers.titleEn: Flexible Phase Change Adhesive Allowing Tunable Melting Point for Flexible Electronics Thermal Management with Controlled Adhesion
papers.abstract: Currently, flexible phase-change materials that have been widely investigated for flexible electronics typically exhibit melting points below 60 °C and lack intrinsic interfacial adhesion. These limitations render them inadequate for thermal management under bending, twisting, and other mechanical deformations encountered in flexible devices. To overcome these constraints, we developed a strategy in which novel urea-based phase-change materials (PCMs) were incorporated in situ into a polyacrylate matrix via a solvent-free UV-curing process, thereby constructing a flexible phase-change adhesive (FPCA) that combines strong interfacial adhesion with a tunable melting point covering 60-100 °C. The optimized FPCA formulation (E90A10-H6U-40 wt %) achieves an exceptional combination of properties: high flexibility (tensile strength: 0.44 MPa; elongation at break: 1227%), melt point (74.2 °C), reliable phase change enthalpy (53.4 J/g), strong adhesion (180° peel force: 5.5 N/25 mm at phase-transition temperature), folding endurance exceeding 200 000 cycles, and stable performance after accelerated aging (85 °C/85% Relative Humidity for 168 h). The FPCA series also enables controlled thermal debonding with debonding ratios exceeding 99%, supporting temporary bonding and non-destructive device recycling. This work substantially broadens the material landscape for flexible thermal management and offers a promising pathway toward next-generation, wearable-compatible electronic devices.
papers.filename: Jianhui Xia, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2026, Flexible Phase Change Adhesive Allowing Tunable Melting Point for Flexible Electronics Thermal Management with Controlled Adhesion

papers.titleEn: UV-Cured Semi-Interpenetrating Polymer Network Electrolyte for High-Performance Bipolar-Stacked Quasi-Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries are regarded as promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to their high energy density. However, electrolyte instability and lithium dendrite formation remain critical challenges. Accordingly, a semi‐interpenetrating polymer network (semi‐IPN) quasi‐solid polymer electrolyte (QSPE) is developed by incorporating polyethylene glycol monomethyl ether methacrylate (PEGMA), polyethylene glycol dimethacrylate (PEGDA), and vinyl ethylene carbonate (VEC) into a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) matrix via UV curing. The prepared semi‐IPN QSPE exhibits a high ionic conductivity of 1.36 × 10 −3 S cm −1 and a Li‐ion transference number of 0.78 at room temperature, while maintaining flexibility with a tensile strength of 5.2 MPa and a Young's modulus of 25.1 MPa. Furthermore, it demonstrates a wide electrochemical stability window up to 4.8 V and excellent interfacial compatibility with a lithium (Li) anode. Based on these properties, bipolar cells, constructed by serially connecting two LFP/QSPE/Li unit cells, not only achieve an open‐circuit voltage of 6.36 V stably, but also deliver a discharge capacity of 144 mAh g −1 at 0.2 C with 77.0% capacity retention and 99.0% coulombic efficiency after 100 cycles.
papers.filename: Dukjoon Kim, Small, 2026, UV-Cured Semi-Interpenetrating Polymer Network Electrolyte for High-Performance Bipolar-Stacked Quasi-Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
